title: Red palm mites on coconut and palm - Grenada

Header: Red palm mites on coconut and palm - Grenada

Prevention: Observe plant quarantine regulations when moving planting material.
Inspect plants for mites prior to movement.
Be aware of the signs and symptoms.
Remove alternate hosts such as ornamentals from coconut field.
Monitoring: Where possible, check the underside of leaves for presence of mites.
A hand lens will be required.
Symptoms start as small yellow spots on the lower surface which become larger and more intense.
Observe leaves for necrotic areas, abnormal colouring and drying.
Lower leaves are more severely affected and may appear yellow.
Abortion of flowers and small nuts follow yellowing of leaves.
Plants can be checked once a week for symptoms or presence of the mites.
Take action when 4-5 lower leaves per plant become necrotic.
Direct Control: Infected lower leaves should be cut, and burnt immediately.
It is very difficult and a waste of money to spray palm trees with insecticides when they are very tall.
Small nursery plants can be sprayed with
Oil: main ingredient soya bean oil. 30ml per 1gal of water.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
